title: "Conclusion"
---

## Key Findings

This project tried to answer one main question. Can computer analysis capture the differences between Brazilian and Russian Phonk? [cite_start]The answer is a clear yes, but there are some important details[cite: 66]. [cite_start]By looking at harmony, loudness, tempo, rhythm, texture, and machine learning, we see a consistent pattern[cite: 67].

---

### What the Analysis Revealed

**1. Harmony is very important for defining these genres, but in opposite ways.**

[cite_start]The chroma analysis showed that Brazilian Phonk does not focus on harmony[cite: 68]. [cite_start]Its energy is spread across all pitches in quick bursts, so there is no main musical key[cite: 68]. [cite_start]On the other hand, Russian Drift Phonk is firmly anchored to a clear F# Minor key the whole time[cite: 69]. [cite_start]This is done on purpose[cite: 70]. [cite_start]Russian producers use harmony to tell a story, while Brazilian producers just use it for sound texture[cite: 70].

**2. Tempo is the biggest difference.**

[cite_start]It is amazing that Brazilian Phonk almost always stays around 130 BPM, especially since the genre has no official rules[cite: 71]. [cite_start]This happened naturally through community feedback and streaming data[cite: 72]. [cite_start]Producers who strayed from 130 BPM simply got fewer streams[cite: 72]. [cite_start]This is a great example of how platform algorithms indirectly shape how a genre sounds[cite: 73]. [cite_start]Meanwhile, Russian Phonk has a very wide tempo range of 80 to 180 BPM[cite: 74]. [cite_start]This makes sense because it started with car-culture video editors[cite: 74]. [cite_start]They needed tracks that felt intense, not tracks that followed standard dance rules[cite: 74].

**3. Rhythm and sound texture show different goals.**

[cite_start]By looking at rhythmic peaks, we can see that Brazilian Phonk keeps a constant wall of sound[cite: 138]. [cite_start]It relies on a non-stop rhythmic loop with no quiet parts or real breaks[cite: 139]. [cite_start]The Russian track breathes a lot more[cite: 148]. [cite_start]It uses quieter intros, slow build-ups, and heavy drops to boost the energy[cite: 143]. We also looked at sound texture over time. [cite_start]Brazilian Phonk keeps the same texture on purpose[cite: 167]. [cite_start]Russian Drift Phonk actually changes its texture to create a sense of movement and drama[cite: 167].

**4. The computer model works, but Russian Phonk is harder to pin down.**

[cite_start]The machine learning model was 90% accurate on our 114 tracks, which is a strong result[cite: 75]. [cite_start]The 10% error rate mostly came from mixing up Russian Phonk tracks[cite: 76]. [cite_start]This is not a failure, but actually a really cool finding[cite: 76]. [cite_start]It shows that Russian Drift Phonk is very open[cite: 77]. [cite_start]It borrows sounds from other genres, including Brazilian Phonk, while still keeping its own vibe[cite: 77]. [cite_start]This is totally normal for an experimental, internet-driven genre that does not have strict rules yet[cite: 78].

### Who Could Benefit From This?

| Audience | Application |
|:---|:---|
| **Streaming platforms** | [cite_start]Better tags and more accurate recommendations for Phonk listeners[cite: 80]. |
| **Music researchers** | [cite_start]A new way to study how online communities change music styles[cite: 81]. |
| **Producers** | [cite_start]Real data on what audio features make each style popular[cite: 82]. |
| **Playlist curators** | [cite_start]A math-based way to separate Brazilian and Russian Phonk for mood playlists[cite: 83]. |

### Reflection

[cite_start]This project completely changed how I think about my own tracks[cite: 84]. [cite_start]Seeing *MONTAGEM REBOLA* as just vertical noise on a chart made a lot of sense[cite: 85]. [cite_start]I realized I made a track with no harmony because the genre's rules simply do not want it[cite: 85]. 

[cite_start]My Brazilian track looks very typical for its genre in the computer data[cite: 86]. However, the Russian track *S.X.N.D. N.X.D.E.S.* is actually pretty unusual for Russian Phonk because it was so easy to classify[cite: 87]. [cite_start]Knowing this gives me a fresh way to look at my own creative choices[cite: 87]. [cite_start]Using computers to study music does not replace actually listening to it, but it does help us see the hidden rules behind what we hear[cite: 88]. [cite_start]This is especially true for Phonk, since it is a genre born on the internet, shaped by algorithms, and defined by community feedback[cite: 89].
